A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SuperVoxelGPT. All 26 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v3, including supplementary material, are readable. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-3D and image-to-3D experiments in Tables 1–2, together with quantitative component ablations in Tables C3–C5.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds parameter-sensitivity results and an original GaussianAnything evaluation in Appendices C and E.

M1.justification: The saliency predictor, CVT partitioning, SuperVoxelVAE, autoregressive objective, and Jacobi decoding remain unchanged, including default K=4 and t=0.1. Fig. 7 changes its model label from Qwen 0.5/1 B to Qwen 0.5B, matching the 0.5B model already specified in v1's text.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Trellis-500K subset, with 10,000 training shapes and 1,000 test shapes, for text- and image-conditioned shape generation. The additions evaluate existing VAE reconstruction under different parameters and another comparator on the retained image-to-shape test set; they introduce no new dataset or population.

E2.justification: Appendix E adds GaussianAnything as an evaluated image-to-shape comparator. The original benchmark and ablation comparators remain. CraftsMans becoming CraftsMan3D in Table 2 corrects naming: v1's Appendix B already specifies the same CraftsMan3D variant.

E3.justification: The added sensitivity experiment retrains 32 SuperVoxelVAE configurations over K=1–8 and t={0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3}, evaluating compression and reconstruction on 1,000 test shapes. GaussianAnything receives TSDF mesh extraction before the existing evaluation protocol. Original splits, metrics, training settings, and default parameters are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially extends analysis of the central compression–fidelity tradeoff: Fig. C1 reports reconstruction error alongside compression across retrained parameter configurations and illustrates failures at larger K. v1's Fig. 5 only showed compression curves. Appendix E adds a GaussianAnything mesh-extraction case study. Existing component ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental results. The 32 added configurations are parameter variants, not repeated runs or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds compression and reconstruction results across 32 configurations, including increasing reconstruction error at larger K. Appendix E newly reports GaussianAnything CDL2=0.0471, PSNR=20.33, ULIP-2 similarity=0.363, and runtime=57.92 seconds, plus a training-cost summary. Tables 1–2 and v1 Tables C3–C5, now D1–D3, retain their numerical results; no same-setting performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: The saliency-to-size mapping, density relation, token-count estimate, CVT update, training objective, and appendix metric definitions are unchanged. Appendix equations are renumbered. Expanded parameter explanations introduce no new derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same representation-first, two-stage framework and plug-in tokenizer claims, including 12.8% token length and approximately 10× inference speedup. Abstract wording about prompts and Trellis-500K data clarifies scope already documented in v1.

C2.justification: v3 explains compression saturation, reconstruction degradation at large K, and the noise-suppression tradeoff controlled by t. Appendix E adds interpretation of Gaussian representations as complementary to mesh generation and discusses future training scalability. The original limitations concerning saliency, detail-rich shapes, textures, and limited training data remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly reports five days of training on eight H100 GPUs, documents GaussianAnything's TSDF conversion, and specifies the sensitivity experiment's configurations and retraining. Fig. 5 now identifies training-data statistics as its source, and Fig. 6 labels iteration counts. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original training procedure.

R1.justification: GaussianAnything is newly cited and discussed as a complementary Gaussian-based approach with different rendering and mesh-extraction strengths. The principal research positioning remains unchanged. Most other reference edits update publication metadata or correct bibliographic details for already cited works.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. v3 expands parameter-selection explanations, inserts supplementary Parameter Sensitivity Analysis and Discussion sections, and renumbers retained appendices. Smaller edits clarify terminology, baseline naming, front matter, and references.

P2.justification: v3 adds Fig. C1, Fig. E3, and Table E4. Fig. 6 gains panel and iteration labels, Fig. 7's model label is corrected, and Fig. 8's montage is refreshed while retaining its examples. Existing supplementary figures and tables are retained and renumbered; the overall visual design is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 justified its default parameters mainly through compression statistics; v3 adds reconstruction-quality evidence for that choice in Fig. C1. The GaussianAnything mesh comparison and disclosed training duration also improve empirical context and transparency. These are useful, bounded gains: the main results remain unchanged, and the training-cost comparison uses differing hardware and settings rather than demonstrating scalability through controlled experiments.
